title: Inventory
text: Inventory ingests one or more source repositories into a knowledge graph — files, functions, types and the relations between them — that you can filter, browse and ask questions of. Like Wikis, it lives at its own Inventory area, addressed by the Inventory toolkit that built the graph. Prerequisites An Inventory toolkit with at least one source added. A source toolkit of an allowed type — by default GitHub or ADO Repos (a deployment can widen this with ELITEA INVENTORY SOURCE TYPES ; GitLab and Bitbucket are not supported as sources even when connected as toolkits elsewhere). An llm model set on the Inventory toolkit — ingestion is refused without one. Build a knowledge graph If the project has none yet, add one — the Inventory area prompts you to when it finds none for the project. Under Sources , add a source toolkit (GitHub or ADO Repos, unless the deployment allows more) and its branch. Select Run ingestion . Progress shows per source: Pending, Ingesting…, Done, or Error. You can Stop ingestion on a source that's running. Browse the graph Filter entities by source, type and layer, and search by name. Select an entity to see its file location and its relations — incoming and outgoing edges to other entities. A source removed from the toolkit but still represented in the graph shows as "No longer configured — its entities are still in the graph," rather than disappearing silently. Ask about the inventory Select Ask this inventory to open a question panel over the graph. Answers name the entities they came from, rather than answering from general knowledge. Statistics and maintenance The Stats view breaks the graph down by layer and entity type, and reports cache size and cached graph count. Maintenance normalizes type name variations (for example "Feature" vs. "feature") and rebuilds the name, type, file and source indices. Common issues Inventory runs on the deployment's engine sidecar, not the Rust/Python agent worker — ingestion and browsing work the same regardless of which worker your deployment runs for agents and toolkits. "This toolkit configures no LLM model, so ingestion is refused" means you must set llm model in the Inventory toolkit's settings before Run ingestion will do anything. If the ingestion status can't be read, the per source states shown are stale, not necessarily current — re check after a refresh rather than assuming a source is still Pending.

title: Wikis (DeepWiki)
text: DeepWiki turns a code repository — or a folder of files in an artifact bucket — into browsable documentation: a page tree, diagrams, and a chat you can ask questions of. It lives at its own Wikis area, addressed by the wiki toolkit that generated it, rather than under Toolkits. DeepWiki needs the deployment's engine image tag and ELITEA DEEPWIKI ENABLED . A deployment on the default image lists and reads existing wikis but refuses every generation request. Prerequisites A wiki toolkit pointed at a source: a Repository (via a GitHub, GitLab or ADO Repos toolkit you've already connected), an Artifact folder , or a Bucket . An llm model and embedding model set on the toolkit, or a project default for both — generation and wiki chat fall back to the project's default model when the toolkit sets none, and refuse outright if the project has none either. Generate a wiki If the project has none yet, add one — the Wikis area prompts you to when it finds none for the project. Under the toolkit's own settings, set the wiki source: a repository toolkit to clone, an artifact folder, or a bucket. Optionally set a folder prefix to scope a bucket or artifact source. Select Generate wiki . Choose a planner mode ( Agentic or Clustering ) and whether to Skip tests , then confirm. Generation can take several minutes and runs one at a time per slot — if all slots are busy, wait or stop another run first. Browse and edit Once generated, browse the page tree, open Edit page to hand correct a page (diagrams that fail to render offer a one click fix you can accept or discard), and use Delete wiki to remove generated pages. Ask about the wiki Select Ask about this repository to open the chat drawer. Every question and answer is saved server side as you go, so closing the drawer or reloading the page does not lose the conversation — reopening it picks the same session back up, and your next question still carries the earlier turns as context. Use the history icon in the drawer's header to see this toolkit's past conversations, resume one, or delete one you no longer need. Clear the conversation starts a fresh session rather than erasing the old one — the previous conversation stays in the history list. You can attach two kinds of context to a question: Wiki pages — pick pages already published in the wiki you're reading; the server resolves the content, so what you attach is always what the wiki actually says. Files from your own machine — the paperclip with a badge control next to it lets you attach small text files (Markdown, plain text, CSV, most source code) up to a few hundred KB each and five files per question. Their content is read in your browser and sent along with the question; nothing is uploaded to the wiki's own pages. Both stay attached across questions in the same session until you remove them. Common issues DeepWiki runs on the deployment's engine sidecar, not the Rust/Python agent worker — generation and wiki chat work the same regardless of which worker your deployment runs for agents and toolkits. "No embedding model is set" or "No llm model is set" warnings mean generation or chat will use the project's default model for that role — and refuse outright if the project has none.

title: Make toolkit tools available by MCP
text: Agents and pipelines reach MCP clients through a tag, but toolkit tools reach them through a per toolkit checkbox: Make tools available by MCP , in the toolkit editor's Tools section. Only the tools you've selected on a flagged toolkit are published; nothing is exposed by default. Expose a toolkit's tools Open an existing toolkit (or create one — see the toolkit's own page under Toolkits), and go to its Tools tab. Choose which of the toolkit's tools should be callable at all (the same selection agents and pipelines use). Check Make tools available by MCP . Elitea publishes one MCP tool per selected tool, named (for example github create issue ). Select Save . The client's next tools/list call picks up the change — reconnect the client if it caches the tool list for the session. How a call runs A tools/call for a published toolkit tool dispatches through the same run path chat uses — with idempotency and polling for the worker's result — not a stub. It still needs the toolkit's own prerequisites: the right worker for that toolkit type, and a working credential. Common issues This only controls MCP exposure — the toolkit still needs to work in ordinary use (the right worker, a valid credential) before its tools will succeed when an MCP client calls them; see the toolkit's own page for that.

title: Elitea MCP server
text: Elitea is itself an MCP server: any client that speaks the Model Context Protocol can call your tagged agents, pipelines and toolkit tools as MCP tools. The transport is streamable HTTP — a single POST endpoint that answers initialize , tools/list and tools/call . There is no SSE stream and no stdio server: a GET on the endpoint answers "The server does not offer an SSE stream at this endpoint." Prerequisites Your project's MCP endpoint: https:// /app/ /mcp . A personal access token, sent as Authorization: Bearer . The server authenticates every request as that token's owner and scopes results to projects they belong to. At least one agent or pipeline tagged mcp , or a toolkit with tools marked "available by MCP" (see Make tools available by MCP) — otherwise tools/list returns an empty, but correct, list. Tag an agent or pipeline for MCP Open the agent or pipeline you want to expose. Add the tag mcp to it. Elitea exposes one tool per tagged agent/pipeline, taking a single free form task string as input. If the agent has several tagged versions, the newest tagged one is the one served — not necessarily the version marked "latest" in the UI. Retag or delete older tagged versions if you need a specific one served. Connect a client Add a server entry to .vscode/mcp.json (workspace) or your user mcp.json (global): Reload the MCP server list, then select tools from your Elitea project in Copilot Chat's Agent mode. Common issues Calling a toolkit tool through this MCP server needs the Python worker's toolkit dispatch — Helm and compose both default to the Python worker ( 865/ 866), and on a deployment that opts into the Rust worker instead, a toolkit tool call answers a protocol error instead of a result. Agent and pipeline tools tagged mcp run the same way on either worker. Two agents that sanitize to the same tool name collapse into one entry in tools/list — whichever the database returns first wins, silently. Give MCP tagged agents and pipelines unique names. A client that opens a GET (SSE) connection to the endpoint gets a 405, not a stream. If your client only supports the older SSE transport, it can't connect here — use a client that speaks streamable HTTP.

title: Pre-built MCP servers
text: An admin can curate a catalogue of MCP servers that every project sees as ready made toolkit tiles, so project members don't each have to look up a URL and register their own OAuth client. This replaces what the legacy docs called "EPAM MCPs" — the mechanism is now vendor neutral; an admin can add any MCP server here, not a fixed list. Add a server to the catalogue As an admin, open Configuration in the admin console and go to the MCP servers section. Select Add MCP server . Give it a display name (its catalogue key is derived from the name, or fixed once other projects reference it) and the server's base URL. If the server needs OAuth and doesn't support Dynamic Client Registration, enter the OAuth client ID and client secret . The secret is sealed into the platform vault immediately — no endpoint ever returns it again, including this form on a later edit. Check Offer this server to projects , then Save . Project members now see it as a tile, the same as a hand added Remote MCP. Common issues A catalogued server is a built in Elitea type, not part of the SDK worker capability catalogue. Both the Rust and Python workers can call its tools — only HTTP based servers can be catalogued in the first place, and that is the only transport either worker's MCP client needs. Removing a catalogued server deletes its stored client secret permanently. To stop offering a server without losing the secret, edit it and clear Offer this server to projects instead of deleting it. Stdio transport MCP servers are refused here — only HTTP based remote servers can be catalogued.

title: Remote MCP
text: Remote MCP is the other direction from the Elitea MCP server: instead of exposing Elitea's tools to an external client, a Remote MCP toolkit lets an Elitea agent or pipeline call tools hosted on someone else's MCP server. It's listed as Remote MCP in the toolkit type picker; there is no local or stdio MCP client — only this HTTP connection. Prerequisites The remote server's URL. If the server requires OAuth: either nothing further (if it supports Dynamic Client Registration) or a pre registered OAuth client ID and secret from that server's own admin console. Connect a remote MCP server In the left navigation, open Toolkits , then select New , and choose Remote MCP . Enter the remote server's URL and save. If the server requires OAuth, Elitea opens an authorization dialog — automatically, either now or the first time an agent tries to call one of its tools. Servers that support Dynamic Client Registration need nothing from you beyond clicking Authorize ; a server that doesn't asks for a Client ID and Client Secret first. The flow uses PKCE or OIDC depending on what the server advertises, and you can choose to remember the credentials for the session. Once authorized, Elitea calls the remote server's tools/list and shows the tools it offers. Attach the toolkit to an agent or pipeline the same way as any other toolkit. Common issues Remote MCP is a built in Elitea type, not part of the SDK worker capability catalogue. Both the Rust and Python workers can call a Remote MCP toolkit's tools — the Rust worker's MCP client only speaks streamable HTTP, which is the only transport a remote server can use here anyway. Authorization can happen mid conversation: if a tool call fails because the session isn't authorized yet, Elitea shows the same authorization dialog from chat. Send your message again once it succeeds. The redirect for the OAuth flow lands on /mcp auth callback . If you're testing behind a proxy or a non default host, make sure that path is reachable at the same origin the browser used to start the flow.

title: API usage
text: Everything the web app does goes through the same REST API you can call directly — from a script, a Power Automate flow, or any HTTP client that can send a bearer token. Authenticate Open Settings › Personal tokens and create a token. Copy it immediately — it's shown once. Add an Authorization: Bearer header. A pylon compatibility alternative, X API Key: , is also accepted. Most endpoints take a project id in the path. A token can only act on projects its owner belongs to. Endpoint layout REST endpoints live under /api/v2/... — the same paths the web app calls. Interactive API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger UI) is served at /api/docs , with the raw spec at /api/openapi.yaml and /api/openapi.json . Both are public — no token needed to read the spec. The MCP server is at /app/{projectID}/mcp (see Elitea MCP server) — the same bearer token authenticates it. SCIM provisioning, for identity providers that push users and groups, is at /api/v2/scim/v2 . It's configured per identity provider under Authentication, not by a personal token. Call the API from Power Automate (or any HTTP client) In your flow, add a generic HTTP (or "HTTP with Azure AD" if you prefer a service account) action. Point it at the /api/v2/... path for the operation you need — check /api/docs for the exact path, parameters and body shape. Set the header to Bearer , stored as a secret in your flow, not inline in plain text. Common issues A token only reaches projects its owner belongs to — a 403 on an otherwise correct call usually means the token owner isn't a member of the project id in the path, not a malformed request. Webhooks (both directions) have a UI now: a pipeline's inbound trigger is configured from the pipeline editor's Triggers & schedules panel, and the project's outbound webhook registry has its own Settings › Webhooks page — see Webhooks and pipeline triggers. Both APIs still work with a personal access token if you'd rather script registration.

title: ADO boards
text: Read and manage Azure DevOps boards: work items, queries and area/iteration paths. It's listed under the project management category in the toolkit type picker. Prerequisites An account at ADO boards with permission to issue an API token or credential, saved in Elitea as a ado credential ( /credentials/create credential/ ). Or skip the saved credential and paste token directly into the toolkit's own settings (inline auth). If you plan to index content for retrieval: a pgvector credential and an embedding model, configured under AI providers. Connect the toolkit In the left navigation, open Toolkits , then select New . Filter the type picker by the project management category, or search for "ADO boards". Under the credential field, choose an existing ado credential, or select Create credential to add one without leaving the form. title: Custom
text: Custom isn't a vendor integration — it's a fallback editor. Every toolkit type normally gets a typed form built from its schema, but Custom always appears at the bottom of the type picker as a generic JSON settings editor you can point at any type. Use it when a type has no typed form yet, or when you need to set a field the form doesn't expose. Custom is added by the web client itself and has no entry in the toolkit type catalogue — there's no fixed tool list or worker verdict to report, because it isn't a type on its own. It edits the settings of whatever underlying toolkit type you choose. Prerequisites The toolkit type key you want to configure (for example github or jira ) and the field names its schema expects — check that type's own page in this catalogue, or the type's settings in the create form first. Any credential the underlying type needs, created the normal way under Credentials. Configure a toolkit as raw JSON In the left navigation, open Toolkits , then select New . Custom is listed at the end of the type picker, outside the category filters. The editor is a JSON text area with syntax highlighting and linting. Enter the type and settings fields the underlying toolkit type expects. Name the toolkit and select Create . Elitea validates the JSON but does not re check it against the target type's schema beyond basic parsing — a field name typo won't be caught here. Available tools There's no fixed tool list — the tools exposed are whatever the underlying toolkit type provides once its settings are valid. Common issues A malformed or incomplete settings object saves without error but fails at call time, not at save time. Prefer the type's own dedicated form when one is available, and reach for Custom only for the fields it's missing.

Most configure a single whitelisted API call rather than a rich tool set, or cover a Zephyr variant that isn't Zephyr Scale or Zephyr Enterprise. Each row below states whether it runs on the Python worker (the default for both Helm and compose, 865/ 866) and the Rust worker (opt in) — see Toolkits for what a greyed out tile means. Cloud and infrastructure Each of these wraps a single provider API in one or two generic call tools; none needs a saved credential beyond what the provider's own client library picks up from the worker's environment, except where noted. | Type | Label | What it does | Auth | Python | Rust | | | | | | | | | aws | Cloud AWS | Runs one whitelisted AWS API call ( execute aws ). | none | No | No | | azure | Cloud Azure | Runs one whitelisted Azure API call, plus a health check. | none | No | Yes | | gcp | Cloud GCP | Runs one whitelisted Google Cloud API request. | none | No | Yes | | k8s | Cloud Kubernetes | Runs one whitelisted kubectl style command, plus a health check. | none | No | Yes | | keycloak | Keycloak | Runs one whitelisted Keycloak admin API request. | none | Yes | Yes | | localgit | Local GIT | Reads, diffs and commits files in a Git checkout the worker can reach on disk. | none | No | No | aws , bigquery , gcp , k8s and localgit fail to import on the Python worker, with no fix tracked for these five, and — except azure / gcp / k8s — are also skipped by the Rust worker (tracked in 865); check both columns before relying on one of these in a fresh install. Filter the tile grid by category (cloud, testing, and so on), or search by name. Types with a saved credential column above need one created first (or inline via Create credential in the form); the rest only take a project/host/namespace style setting. Name the toolkit and select Create . Common issues A type whose worker column says No for your deployment doesn't error loudly — its tile is simply absent from the picker ( metadata.hidden=true ). If a type you expect is missing, check which worker the deployment runs before assuming it doesn't exist.
